Technical & Consumer Questions Answered • v0.5.0

Frequently Asked Questions

Clear, honest answers about Dual-Layer Microsoft Azure Artifact Signing, why our universal installer targets 64-bit x64 and ARM64 (skipping extinct IA-64 and 32-bit x86 host OS builds while still supporting legacy 32-bit app payloads), plain-English setup tiers, accessibility, and our official four-edition lineup (Community == Architect parity).

Part 1 • Downloads, Authenticode Signing & Supported Processors

Code Signing, CPU Detection & Architecture Choices

1. Why does Windows SmartScreen still warn on v0.5.0 even though the downloads are cryptographically signed?

Every v0.5.0 installer and inner executable is 100% Authenticode-signed via Microsoft Azure Artifact Signing under verified Public Trust identity (Michael Ragsdale, chaining to Microsoft Identity Verification Root Certificate Authority 2020 with RFC 3161 SHA-256 timestamps from http://timestamp.acs.microsoft.com and verified via signtool verify /pa).

Why SmartScreen still prompts temporarily: Since mid-2024, Microsoft retired automatic Day-1 SmartScreen bypasses for all newly issued certificates (including EV and cloud HSM keys). Because our Azure Artifact Signing identity went live on November 25, 2026, Windows Defender SmartScreen displays “Windows protected your PC” until initial download reputation builds and Microsoft Security Intelligence (WDSI) completes its review of our submitted v0.5.0 binaries (which are hash-frozen on the CDN during review).

How to verify authenticity before running: Click More info on the SmartScreen dialog and confirm Windows displays Publisher: Michael Ragsdale before clicking Run anyway.

2. I don't know whether my Windows PC is AMD64 (x64) or ARM64. Which file do I download?

Either of our two universal buttons works on both Intel/AMD x64 and Snapdragon / Windows on ARM ARM64 computers automatically:

  • Smart Web Setup (raggiesoft-installer-studio-setup.exe, ~862 KB): Queries IsWow64Process2 at launch (piercing Windows 11 Prism emulation in under 0.1ms), downloads only your processor's native signed installer over HTTPS, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and runs it natively.
  • Full Offline Universal Installer (raggiesoft-installer-studio-offline-setup.exe, ~3.9 MB): Packs both signed x64 and ARM64 native installers inside one portable file for offline or air-gapped PCs and USB drives.

3. Why are IA-64 (Itanium) and 32-bit x86 host OS builds skipped?

Every supported Windows desktop, laptop, and workstation in late 2026 runs a 64-bit operating system kernel (IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_AMD64 0x8664 or IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_ARM64 0xAA64):

  • IA-64 (Intel Itanium) is museum hardware: Skipping Itanium lets instbuild.exe strictly guard against emitting PID_TEMPLATE = Intel64;1033 (which meant Itanium and causes msiexec on Intel Core and AMD Ryzen PCs to reject the MSI!), using strictly x64;1033 and Arm64;1033 instead.
  • 32-bit x86 Windows OS is retired: Windows 11 has never shipped a 32-bit operating system image, and 32-bit Windows 10 reached End of Support in October 2025.

4. Can a 64-bit Installer Studio still package legacy 32-bit applications (such as classic Visual Basic 6.0 programs)?

Yes! Skipping 32-bit host OS builds does not prevent a 64-bit instbuild.exe from packaging legacy 32-bit payload applications running via SysWOW64. Our v0.8.0 milestone includes a Visual Basic 6.0 (.vbp) Importer emitting Intel;1033 metadata and zero-elevation Reg-Free COM side-by-side manifests.

Part 2 • Setup Types, Inclusion Tiers, Editions & AI Agents

Plain-English Authoring, Accessibility & Official Product Editions

5. What is "Included In" (Minimal, Typical, Complete) vs. Windows Installer InstallLevel?

RaggieSoft Installer Studio replaces cryptic numeric Feature.Level thresholds with plain-English Included In tiers (minimal, typical, complete, and hidden) paired with classic Typical / Compact / Complete / Custom or modern Express / Compact / Custom Setup Types!

6. How do Community, Essentials, Developer, and Architect editions compare—and is Community really 100% Architect parity?

Yes, permanently. Community Edition (free for hobbyists, solo creators, students, educators, and open source) maintains 100% technical feature parity with Architect Edition with zero watermarks. For commercial teams, Essentials covers guided .MSI + Setup.exe, sfx self-extractors, .MSM consumption, and Major Upgrades; Developer adds .MSM creation, RaggieScript (.rssc), custom dialog designers, and CI/CD agents; and Architect adds .rsis Suites, .MSP binary-delta patches, and HTML5 VPAT 2.5. View the full Editions Matrix →

7. How do AI coding agents use Installer Studio?

.rsip projects and .rsis suites are diff-friendly plain-text INI manifests whose comments survive GUI saves byte-for-byte. Coding agents read our compiler-emitted /installer-studio/llms-full.txt and SKILL.md specs and lint manifests via instbuild.exe --validate --diagnostics=json.

8. Can I stamp outer Setup.exe as asInvoker, highestAvailable, or requireAdministrator—and what if UAC is turned off?

Yes (planned in v0.5.1): [Package] RequestedExecutionLevel gives you a direct choice of asInvoker (default just-in-time elevation on Install), highestAvailable, or requireAdministrator (0.0s launch elevation) stamped into the outer Setup.exe manifest. And even if UAC is completely disabled on the PC (EnableLUA = 0), SetupWizard.exe still verifies true BUILTINAdministrators rights via Win32 CheckTokenMembership (plus MSI Privileged checks) whenever Scope = machine!
